title: Improving the Efficiency of In-Memory-Computing Macro with a Hybrid Analog-Digital Computing Mode for Lossless Neural Network Inference
problem: Analog in-memory-computing (IMC) suffers from large interface circuit overhead that limits its practical energy efficiency gains. Reducing this overhead while maintaining inference accuracy requires rethinking the computation approach.
motivation: Analog IMC offers superior energy efficiency for machine learning workloads, but interface circuit overhead currently restricts its practical adoption and efficiency benefits.
method: In-memory computing stores data and performs math in the same location to save energy, but the circuits connecting analog and digital parts add significant overhead. This paper proposes a hybrid approach: a nonlinear transfer function (a mathematical rule) automatically decides whether each multiplication should happen in the analog domain (fast but less precise) or the digital domain (slower but more accurate), based on the size of the values being multiplied. Small values use analog circuits for efficiency, while large values use digital circuits to maintain accuracy. This eliminates the need for expensive, high-precision interface circuits everywhere—they're only needed where precision actually matters.
key_novelty: A nonlinear transfer function automatically chooses between analog and digital computation modes for each operation based on value size, eliminating expensive interface circuits as the efficiency bottleneck.
contributions: Hybrid analog-digital computing macro architecture for improved efficiency
Nonlinear transfer function for mode selection based on MAC statistics
Reduced interface circuit precision requirements without accuracy loss
2.92× energy efficiency improvement over conventional analog IMC designs
